Episode 163. Returning to the Family (3)
February 25, 1803, early dawn.
Jin was preparing to head towards the Sword Garden, just as they had anticipated.
He even advertised to the entire world through Dino Jaglun that he would be returning to the Sword Garden on February 25.
Furthermore, the special report that Dino personally put out subtly hinted that Jin would be ascending to the position of 'Family Head'.
This was nothing less than a declaration of war towards Lun Kandell.
"Do you think Kinzelo and Ziepfel will really participate in the battle?"
Talaris asked.
The colleagues next to her looked at her and Jin alternately with worried looks.
"They will definitely come. If they can't read such a big opportunity, they don't deserve to be in the command of a major force."
Jin did not plan the participation of the two major forces from the start.
Even when he decided to visit Lun Kandell two weeks ago, Jin was not certain, but seeing how Lun Kandell responded to the return of the knight, it became clear.
The fact that the Prophet had already taken over the family.
And also the fact that Kinzelo and Ziepfel were not provoking the Sword Garden because they presumed Lun Kandell had enough power to feel burdensome.
So, Jin made a risky move.
He decided that he had to create a big picture that, if they weren't idiots, they would have to follow.
"Even if the leaders of the enemies are much more stupid than I think and do not come, it is right for me to go. Even thinking about the people within the family who may be resisting the prophet."
He had never relied on or expected the filthy power of the Prophet.
Those who advise him to the end, the real knights of Lun Kandell, and his brothers, they must be suffering in the Sword Garden.
It was impossible for him not to go to them.
In addition, seeing the article about Temer that Lun Kandell put out, it's possible that Valeria might have been captured.
"As I mentioned before, now is the right time when the family doesn't know about my power."

"Huh, well... yeah. With the military power the son-in-law has now, even if things go wrong, escape should be sufficient. This is, you said it wouldn't take a long time to get to 10 stars, but you might come back stronger than me. Can this happen?"
"That's not the case. You're giving me too much credit. And if Talaris hadn't helped, I would have considered other methods. Since we have Mot and the Red Owl, it's a viable choice."
"Yeah, yeah. Living long enough, even this Talaris Endorma has become nothing more than someone's mode of transportation."
As Talaris laughed, Jin also chuckled while shrugging his shoulders.
The two of them now looked like close colleagues rather than superior and subordinate.
To his surprise, Sirius found that he didn't mind the sight as much as he thought he would.
"Jin."
"Yes, Sirius."
"Our Bi-Gung has protected you countless times over the years, now it's your turn to protect Bi-Gung."
Jin didn't answer but met Sirius's gaze for a moment.
"So, don't go and die, but come back. You have to pay back the debt. I need to teach you some swordsmanship too."
"Of course, I promise rapid growth."
"Our daughter is surprisingly talking about adult matters."
"Mother, be careful too. Don't push yourself too hard with your unhealthy body."
"Young Master...."
Gilli put his hand on Jin's shoulder.
"Please, come back safely."
"As soon as you return, you'll be in a forced march without rest. Lord, I'm sorry for not being able to help."
"Master Jin... are you really okay going alone?"
The colleagues, with Gilli in the center, were worried about Jin.
Talaris sighed as if the scene was frustrating.

"Ugh, really. The son-in-law is not at a level you guys need to worry about anymore, okay? So don't act like Jin is going to die. I would rather see that scoundrel locked up in the laboratory over there."
Kwaul was engrossed in his research, as if he didn't care whether Jin went to Lun Kandell alone or not.
He was completely absorbed in the items Jin brought from Lafrarosa.
These were data that a magic engineer would want to acquire, even if they had to sell their soul.
The only regret was that Valeria, who could share this happiness, was absent.
"Just like Talaris said, don't worry too much. I will return. In the unlikely event that I do not return within three days, be sure to prepare for evacuation."
"In the end, even our son-in-law is adding unnecessary words. Now go, let's go!"
Jin boarded the Red Owl.
"I'll be back. As always, I'll bring back what I want."
The Garden of Swords, revered and feared by all warriors that ever existed in the world, had been the base of Lun Kandell's swordsmen for over a thousand years.
In the middle of it, Rosa stood still.
Her face was pale, and her lips were chapped.
Looking frail and emaciated, she looked hardly like the Black Leopard of Lun Kandell, who had been ruling the family with Shiron. She raised her head and looked at the sky.
The sun was burning, not fitting the winter season.
Even facing it directly, Rosa did not feel her pupils burning.
She merely felt it was unnecessarily bright.
"The youngest... is coming."
A woman in a black hood nodded.
Ilina Lun Kandell, known as the unfortunate companion of Joshua.
Now, everyone in Lun Kandell knew who she was.
The prophet of disaster, who saved the members of Lun Kandell, including Rosa, from chaos.
"Do you sound regretful? Do you think the situation would have changed if you had been a little faster?"
Whoosh!
In an instant, Rosa drew out her madness and stabbed Ilina's throat.
Ilina immediately drew her last breath and fell, convulsing for a few seconds, then she showed signs of getting up again.
Chaos flowed from the wound instead of blood.
"Oh, really. How many times do I have to explain that this does not cost a human life each time?"
"It is impossible for a member of Lun Kandell to speak to me like that. Even if this was your last life, I would not have hesitated to kill you."
"You could have warned me nicely....."
"Do you want to die again? The pain of death is something I have felt, and it is not a light matter for you either."
At Rosa's low voice, Ilina bowed her head.
"I'm sorry, I'll be more careful in the future."
Rosa silently looked at the main gate again.
The main gate.
Looking back, for Rosa Lun Kandell, that gate represented countless lonely years of waiting.
How terribly, fervently she had awaited the day when Shiron, having completed his mission, would return through that gate and save the family...
But that day never came.
Instead, what was certain to come was her youngest son, who absolutely refused to bend or compromise, and whom she would have no choice but to break herself.
That fact tasted a bit bitter.
"Prepare all the former knights of Lun Kandell to greet the family's 12th generation."
Rosa's words are like the wind, stern.
There is no place they do not spread to, however small, and there is no one who does not hear. Just like Shiron's voice was.
Knights from all around the hall came running and lined up before her.
It was just as it had been when the family prepared for Shiron's hospitalization.
The generations stood at the front, followed by the Black Knights, the Black Sword Society, the Executive Knights, and the Guardian Knights.
It was a number far beyond the scene Jin remembered, but there were only four generations.
"Knight Rosa."
It was Stan, the captain of the Black Knights.
"Speak."
"What should we do with the knights in the basement?"
The knights in the basement, they were the ones who had raised their flags to Rosa until the end.
"Release everyone except the 4th generation."
"Understood. And... can we return their weapons?"
The reason Stan spoke like that was no different.
Even though they have now turned their backs on Rosa and the family, they were all knights who once dedicated themselves to the family.
Their rejection of Rosa is not betrayal.
They just couldn't overcome the logic of power and defeat that Rosa came to possess.
So Stan wanted to give them one last chance.
A chance to fight while realizing the 'honor' they think of, along with Jin.
Ilina tried to raise her voice as if she was mad at his words, but Rosa didn't dislike such Stan.
There needed to be such a person.
"Do so. Also, all their swords will be planted in the garden."
"......Thank you."
"May I dare to say a word? I think it's dangerous. Jin Lun Kandell's destiny has already deviated once. Even the smallest factor can be a big problem!"
Rosa silenced her opinion.
And she began to focus on the energy of her youngest son, who was rapidly approaching from afar.
Remembering the day when Jin finished the preliminary generation process and first returned to the family.
"It seems there's another one who would welcome this old man."
"Head of the family, what do you mean by that?"
"Rosa, you've become desensitized too. Quite a powerful energy is approaching the Sword Garden, at a very fast pace."
'So now you see the things you felt back then... Shiron.'
Impressive.
The first emotion that filled Rosa's chest was no different from Shiron's at that time.
Slowly, the main gate was opening.
Jin, despite the appearance of the changed family and the chaotic knights' dark energy, stepped boldly towards Rosa.
As the distance narrowed, both of them felt as if all the surrounding scenery was being erased.
Among these numerous humans and non-human entities, the mother and son focused all their senses on each other.
Everything was the same as that day.
The day when Jin blocked Shiron's sword attack, proving his eligibility to become a generation.
But today is not that day.
"The 12th generation Jin Lun Kandell has returned to the family after completing his solitary training."
Jin didn't raise his sword in salute.
Rosa, without responding, quietly looked down at Jin.
As a Lun Kandell, as a human, as a mother, she wanted to hold onto this brief last moment when she could face her youngest a little longer.
So, just like Shiron did that day, she wanted to draw her sword.
She wanted to taste her son's grown sword by crossing swords just once.
But Jin did not allow that time to extend.
"But mother... you broke your promise with me."
Disappointing.
You no longer have the right to test me.
As Jin continued his words, Rosa unknowingly stopped her hand that was going to her waist.
That was the last touch Rosa felt as a human.
A single stream of black blood flowed between Rosa's parted lips.
Wiping the blood with the back of her hand, she replied.
"The promise is still valid. If you can show here what you promised to prove to me, I'll restore everything of the family right now."
